task_snapshot.title: snake_case splits acronyms into single letters
task_snapshot.description: snake_case inserts an underscore before every uppercase letter, so acronyms such as HTTP or ID are shredded into one-letter words.
task_snapshot.problem_statement:
`textkit.case.snake_case` splits acronyms into single letters.

Reproduction:

    >>> from textkit.case import snake_case
    >>> snake_case("HTTPServer")
    'h_t_t_p_server'

Expected: 'http_server'

Required behaviour:

- A run of consecutive uppercase letters belongs to one word. An uppercase letter starts a new word only when it follows a lowercase letter or a digit, or when it follows another uppercase letter and is itself followed by a lowercase letter (in that case it is the first letter of the next word).
- So `XMLHttpRequest` becomes `xml_http_request` and `userID` becomes `user_id`.
- Spaces, hyphens and underscores still separate words. The result is lowercase, never contains two underscores in a row, and never starts or ends with an underscore.

Existing behaviour covered by `tests/test_case.py` (camelCase, PascalCase, spaces and hyphens, input that is already snake_case) must not change. Keep the function signature.
acceptance_criteria: Acronyms stay together as one word (HTTPServer -> http_server)
An acronym followed by a capitalised word is split before that word's first letter
An uppercase letter after a digit starts a new word
No double, leading or trailing underscores
Existing tests in tests/test_case.py continue to pass
hints: Look at the characters on both sides of an uppercase letter before deciding to insert an underscore.
